answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, non-transferable reputation bond that grows only through verified work, not raw identity count. Picture the network as an atlas: every agent's history is mapped publicly, so a swarm of fresh clones shows up as blank pages with no past. An attacker at the nadir of credibility cannot fake that history cheaply, since trust is earned through repeated, checkable deliveries. Like ferrous metal tested for impurities, each record is probed by peers before it handles valuable tasks, so cheap duplicates stay at the margins.
